sources.method_note: Longest HARD-only path over 21 phase nodes; SOFT edges excluded. Recompute implemented locally without importing claim_record.recompute_schedule_after_soft_1_2.

soft_reclassification.rationale: PHASE-GRAPH edge_semantics: HARD means Phase 2 cannot start until Phase 1 produced a named artifact or Phase 2 output is void without it; SOFT means Phase 2 can start and produce valid output first. The authored HARD reason is that Phase 2 needs every material claim to carry lineage/confidence/verification-path — i.e. an defined claim-record format. CONTESTED-1 settling experiment: author provisional claim-record schema and schema-check a Phase-2 research output; if Phase 2 can emit a conformant record without any Phase-1 corpus output, the edge is SOFT. Provisional schema exists (PROVISIONAL, superseded_by ARC-0085) and covers all ten Phase-1 fields (claim_id, canonical_mechanism, duplicate_of, supports, contradicts, source_lineage, confidence, verification_status, implementation_impact, settling_probe). A synthetic Phase-2 research record with no Phase-1 registry dependency validates against claim-record.provisional.v1.schema.json via Draft202012Validator. Therefore 1->2 reclassifies HARD->SOFT. On-disk edges[] left unchanged; flip is in-memory for schedule math only.

notes: Independent reviewer (2) re-derived schedule from PHASE-GRAPH edges[] and allocation_buckets without accepting the author schedule claim text. Numbers match schedule-recompute.json. Separately, CONTESTED-1 settling experiment passes: provisional schema pull-forward lets a Phase-2 unit emit a conformant claim record with no Phase-1 corpus artifact, so 1->2 is SOFT. Did not invent SUCCESS; did not write schema review; receipt stays BLOCKED; did_not_promote=true.
